title: Provenance source markup: text form and interpretation-string vectors
description: Vectors for the text form of an HTML source string (section 4) and for the check that an interpretation string is text (section 3, PM-2). Every '<', '>' and '&' in this file is written as a JSON escape (\u003c, \u003e, \u0026), so the file holds no literal markup: decode the JSON to get the strings.

format.textForm: source is a source string as published, read as HTML. text is its text form. Compare code point for code point.
format.check: value is an interpretation string. verdict is text when no '<' in it is followed by an ASCII letter, '/', '!' or '?', and markup otherwise.
format.interpretationTextPattern: The same check as a JSON Schema pattern (ECMA-262): a string matches it exactly when its verdict is text.

textForm.shows: Text with no markup and no references is unchanged.
Whitespace is not normalised: the text form removes markup and decodes references, nothing else.
A '<' followed by a space is text.
A '<' followed by a digit is text.
A '<' followed by '=' is text.
A '<' at the end of the string is text.
Only an ASCII letter after '<' opens a tag; a non-ASCII letter does not.
A '>' on its own is text.
A link keeps its text and loses its target. The target survives only in raw.
Block tags and a comment are removed.
Removed tags leave nothing, so text either side of a block boundary joins (open question 1).
A line break tag also leaves nothing (open question 1).
Comments are removed before tags, so a '>' inside a comment does not end it early.
An unterminated comment is not removed as a comment; the tag rule removes its '<' alone.
A tag with no closing '>' loses its '<' alone and keeps the text after it.
Tag names are matched without regard to case.
'</' opens markup even with no name.
'<?' opens markup.
Removing an inner tag can form an outer one; removal repeats until nothing changes.
Three levels deep: each pass forms the next tag, so a fixed number of passes is not enough.
A tag broken by an inner tag is removed through the first '>'; the '>' left after it is text.
A named reference decodes to its character: here U+00A0, which is kept, not turned into a space.
& decodes to '&'.
Decimal numeric references decode.
Hexadecimal numeric references decode.
Numeric references in the C1 range decode as the HTML standard maps them (128 is the euro sign).
A numeric reference to U+0000 decodes to U+FFFD, as in HTML.
A numeric reference to a surrogate decodes to U+FFFD, as in HTML.
A numeric reference to a control character decodes to it, as in HTML. Some HTML decoders drop it instead; this vector catches that.
A numeric reference to a noncharacter decodes to it, as in HTML. Some HTML decoders drop it instead; this vector catches that.
A legacy named reference without ';' decodes, as HTML does in text.
The longest legacy name that prefixes the text decodes; the rest stays.
'&' before a name that is not a reference stays as it is.
An escaped '<' that is text decodes to '<' and stays.
Escaped markup decodes to markup and is then removed.
An escaped comment decodes to a comment and is then removed whole.
References are decoded once: a doubly escaped tag leaves as escaped text (open question 2).
